name: Hope
desc: Found shivering in a storm drain, now the gentlest soul you'll meet.
story: When we found Hope she was hiding from the rain, too frightened to come out. Months of patience later, she leans her whole weight against you for cuddles and walks like a dream on the lead. She asks for very little — a warm spot, a slow walk, and someone to come home to.

name: Biscuit
desc: All wags and wonky ears. Wants to be everyone's best friend.
story: Biscuit greets every morning like it's the best news he's ever heard. He's playful, affectionate, and brilliant with children and other dogs. A garden and a family who like a bit of adventure would make him the happiest dog alive.

name: Little Pip
desc: Tiny, shy, and braver every single day.
story: Pip arrived underweight and wary of hands. She's not quite ready for a home yet, but every day she trusts a little more — a wagging tail here, a gentle nose-bump there. We're taking it at her pace, and when she's ready, she'll be ready for someone very special.

name: Daisy
desc: Clever as a whip and devoted to the bone.
story: Daisy knows her commands, loves a puzzle, and would thrive with someone who wants a thinking companion for long walks and quiet evenings. She bonds deeply and gives back every ounce of love she's shown.

name: Bear
desc: A big gentle giant mending a sore leg and a tender heart.
story: Bear was found as a stray with an injured leg. He's healing well and, despite everything, he's never stopped trusting people. Soon he'll be ready to show some lucky family just how much love a big dog can hold.

name: Willow
desc: Now napping in a sunny living room in Germany.
story: Willow waited a long time, but the right family came. She flew to Germany last winter and now spends her days on long forest walks and her evenings curled by the fire. A perfect ending — and proof of why we do this.

name: Ziggy
desc: Found his forever people in Canada.
story: Ziggy is living his best life in Canada with two kids who adore him and a backyard built for zoomies. From frightened street dog to family member — this is the happy ending every dog deserves.
